title: Shenzhen, Part 1: The County by the Sea
description:
Thomas and Clara drift back through sixteen centuries on the coast that became Shenzhen: Nantou and the salt fields, the walled towns of 1394, Xin'an county, the Great Clearance, Hakka and Cantonese villages, the Opium Wars and the new Hong Kong border, and the little railway market town called Shenzhen. Part 1 of 3.

Chapters: 1. Settling in; 2. The edge of the delta; 3. Nantou, the old seat; 4. Walls against the pirates; 5. Xin'an, a new county; 6. The great clearance; 7. Hakka and Cantonese villages; 8. Ships on the horizon; 9. A railway and a market town; 10. Not just a fishing village; 11. Goodnight.

title: Babylon: City of the Gate of the Gods
description: Henry and Clara drift through Babylon on the Euphrates: clay tablets and cuneiform, Hammurabi's laws, Nebuchadnezzar's city, the blue Ishtar Gate, the ziggurat and the star-watchers, a quiet day on the rooftops, the mystery of the Hanging Gardens, Cyrus and Alexander, and the city that faded into legend. Ancient Cities, 1 of 4.

title: Petra: The Rose-Red City of the Desert
description: Henry and Clara walk the Siq into Petra: the Nabataeans and the incense caravans, the Treasury and its legend, a city carved in stone, water saved in the desert, fine painted pottery, the Monastery at sunset, Rome and the earthquakes, and Burckhardt's quiet rediscovery. Ancient Cities, 3 of 4.

title: Teotihuacan: The Place Where the Gods Were Born
description: Henry and Clara walk the Avenue of the Dead in the high valley of Mexico: a city whose own name is lost, the Pyramids of the Sun and Moon, the Feathered Serpent and its glittering hidden tunnel, apartment compounds and painted walls, a quiet morning at the grinding stone, links to the Maya, the great fire, and Aztec pilgrims among the ruins. Ancient Cities, 4 of 4.

title: Athens: City of Athena and the Olive
description: Henry and Clara climb the Acropolis: Athena's olive tree, the birth of democracy, the Persian wars, Pericles and the Parthenon, the festival of Athena, the harbour and the long walls, theatre and Socrates, war and plague, and the Parthenon's many lives. Ancient Cities, 2 of 4.

title: Shenzhen, Part 2: A River, a Fence, an Experiment
description: Henry and Clara follow Shenzhen from 1949 to 1992: a quiet border town on the railway, two very different sides of a river, Yuan Geng's circle on the map at Shekou, the 1980 Special Economic Zone, 'Shenzhen speed', Deng's 1984 visit, the second-line fence, villages that grew upward, first land auctions and young companies, and the 1992 Southern Tour. Part 2 of 3.

title: Shenzhen, Part 3: The City of Arrivals
description: Henry and Clara follow Shenzhen from 1992 to today: millions of young arrivals and factory dormitories, 'once you come, you are a Shenzhener', the 1997 Hong Kong handover, the stalls of Huaqiangbei, Huawei, BYD, Tencent and DJI, some harder chapters, Futian's towers and Lotus Hill, electric buses and the bay, the painters of Dafen, the end of the second line, and Shekou and old Nantou today. Part 3 of 3.

title: Machu Picchu, Part 1: The Earth-Shaker's Estate in the Clouds
description:
Part 1 of 3. Henry and Clara drift up to the misty ridge between the old peak and the young peak, and meet Pachacuti, "the one who turns the world." Who the Inca were, how Machu Picchu is tied to Pachacuti's royal estate (a 1568 Spanish record of his lands at "Picchu"), the 2021 radiocarbon dates that suggest people lived there by about 1420, and how the builders tamed the rain with buried drainage, layered terraces, a spring-fed canal and sixteen stepped fountains. Terrace restorer Tomás phones in softly. Uncertain history (dates, the original name, population) is gently marked as debated. Quiet mountain wind, a distant stream and a soft Andean flute between chapters.
Next: Part 2, inside the city. Part 3, the quiet years, Bingham in 1911, and Machu Picchu today.

Chapters: 1. Settling In; 2. The Ridge Between Two Peaks; 3. The People of the Sun; 4. Pachacuti, the Earth-Shaker; 5. An Estate in the Clouds; 6. When Was It Built?; 7. How Do You Build on a Mountain?; 8. A Call from the Terraces; 9. The Water That Still Flows; 10. Planning the City; 11. Slowly Down the Mountain.

title: Machu Picchu, Part 2: Inside the City in the Clouds
description:
Part 2 of 3. Henry and Clara walk slowly through Machu Picchu: in through the main gate, to the curved Temple of the Sun and its June-solstice window, the quiet cave below, the royal rooms by the first fountain, the quarry, the Sacred Plaza and the Temple of the Three Windows, and the carved Intihuatana (whose name and purpose are still debated). Then the people: a 2023 ancient-DNA study shows the estate's attendants came from all over the Inca world, from the coast to the Amazon. A gentle imagined day on the ridge, the Temple of the Condor, and out along the Inca roads to the Sun Gate. Next: Part 3, the quiet centuries and how the world came to hear of it.

Chapters: 1. Settling In; 2. Through the Main Gate; 3. The Temple of the Sun; 4. The Royal Rooms; 5. The Quarry and the Sacred Plaza; 6. The Intihuatana; 7. The Main Plaza and the Sacred Rock; 8. Who Lived Here?; 9. A Day on the Ridge; 10. The Condor and the Moon; 11. The Roads Out; 12. Slowly Down the Mountain.

title: Machu Picchu, Part 3: The Quiet Centuries
description:
Part 3 of 3. Henry and Clara follow Machu Picchu from the fall of the Inca empire to today: the epidemic and civil war, Pizarro and Cajamarca, Manco Inca's last refuge at Vilcabamba, and why the estate emptied with no sign the Spanish ever found it. Cusco rebuilt on Inca walls. Three quiet centuries of forest and farmers, early maps, the debated Berns story, and Agustín Lizárraga's charcoal "1902" on the Temple of the Three Windows. Then the damp morning of 24 July 1911: Melchor Arteaga, Sergeant Carrasco, the Richarte and Álvarez families, a local boy leading Hiram Bingham to the ruins, and the real Vilcabamba he walked past. Who gets the credit, Yale's century-long hold on the artifacts and their return to Cusco's Casa Concha, and Machu Picchu now: UNESCO, timed tickets, llamas, orchids and spectacled bears. Debated points (the city's original name, Berns, why it was abandoned) are gently flagged. Next on Slow History: Pompeii.

Chapters: 1. Settling In; 2. The Empire Breaks; 3. The Last Inca Refuge; 4. Cusco Under New Rulers; 5. The Quiet Centuries; 6. A Damp Morning in July; 7. Digging and Telling; 8. Who Gets the Credit?; 9. The Long Way Home; 10. Machu Picchu Today; 11. Goodnight, Machu Picchu.

title: Pompeii: The Town Beneath the Mountain
description:
A single narrator tells the story of Pompeii, the Roman town on the Bay of Naples. It begins with the eruption of Vesuvius in AD 79 and the eyewitness letters of Pliny the Younger, including the death of his uncle, Pliny the Elder, at Stabiae. Then the debate over the date: August or October? After that the episode slows into the centuries the town lay buried, its rediscovery, Fiorelli's plaster casts and the site today. It ends in quiet daily life: the streets, fountains and bakeries, the election notices and graffiti, the baths and amphitheatre, the houses and gardens, and evening on the bay.

Chapters: 1. A Town Beneath the Mountain; 2. The Mountain; 3. The Letters of Pliny; 4. Darkness at Misenum; 5. What the Volcano Did; 6. Which Day?; 7. Asleep for Centuries; 8. The Shapes in the Ash; 9. Pompeii Today; 10. Streets, Water and Bread; 11. Walls That Talk; 12. Temples, Baths and Games; 13. Houses and Gardens; 14. Evening on the Bay.

title: Angkor: The City in the Forest
description:
A single narrator tells the story of Angkor, the great capital of the Khmer Empire in Cambodia. It begins with the Cham attack of 1177 and the rise of Jayavarman VII, who built Angkor Thom and the Bayon with its calm stone faces. Then the long, gradual fading of the capital, where historians still debate the causes. After that the episode goes back to the beginnings: Phnom Kulen, the brick towers of Roluos, and the barays and canals revealed by lidar. It goes on to the island shrine of Neak Pean, Banteay Srei, Angkor Wat and its carvings, and the account of the Chinese envoy Zhou Daguan. It ends in daily life and evening among the temples.

Chapters: 1. The City in the Forest; 2. Fire on the Lake; 3. A New Capital; 4. The Long Fading; 5. Never Quite Lost; 6. Beginnings on the Mountain; 7. The Sacred Bull; 8. Water; 9. The Island in the Pool; 10. The Citadel of Women; 11. The Temple of Vishnu; 12. Stories in Stone; 13. A Visitor from China; 14. Daily Life; 15. Evening at Angkor.

title: Alexandria: The Library by the Sea
description:
A single narrator tells the story of the Library of Alexandria. It begins with the question of how the library ended: Caesar's fire, Aurelian's war, the Serapeum, Hypatia and a later legend. None of these alone tells the whole story. Then the debate over how many books it held. After that the episode goes back to Alexander's founding of the city, its streets and harbours, the Pharos lighthouse, and the Museum and its scholars, from Callimachus's catalogue to Eratosthenes measuring the Earth. Later it visits the Serapeum, the catacombs of Kom el Shoqafa, the papyri of Oxyrhynchus and the new Bibliotheca Alexandrina. It ends with evening on the harbour.

Chapters: 1. A Library by the Sea; 2. How Did It End?; 3. How Many Books?; 4. The City of Alexander; 5. Streets of Alexandria; 6. The Lighthouse; 7. The Museum; 8. Collecting the World; 9. The Librarians; 10. Measuring the Earth; 11. Scholars of the Museum; 12. The Temple of Serapis; 13. The Last of the Ptolemies; 14. Beneath the City; 15. Books in the Sand; 16. The New Library; 17. Evening on the Harbour.

title: The Great Wall: Many Walls
description:
A single narrator tells the story of the Great Wall of China, which is really many walls built over two thousand years. It begins with the Ming frontier's most dramatic moments: the capture of an emperor at Tumu in 1449, Altan Khan's raid of 1550 and the peace that followed, and the opening of Shanhaiguan in 1644. Then it goes back to rammed-earth walls, the Qin and Han frontiers, and soldiers' letters on wooden strips. After that come the beacon towers, the walls between the dynasties, the Cloud Platform at Juyongguan, Qi Jiguang's brick towers, and travellers such as Xuanzang and the Macartney embassy. It also covers Jiayuguan and a few myths, including whether the Wall is visible from space. It ends with evening on a quiet stretch of the wall.

Chapters: 1. Many Walls; 2. The Emperor Who Was Captured; 3. Raiders at the Gates; 4. The Gate by the Sea; 5. Earth Between Boards; 6. The Han Frontier; 7. Letters on Wood; 8. Signals Across the Hills; 9. Between the Dynasties; 10. Soldiers from the South; 11. Brick and Stone; 12. Travellers at the Gates; 13. A Few Old Stories; 14. The Fortress in the West; 15. The Wall Today; 16. Walking the Wall; 17. Along the Line; 18. Evening on the Wall.

title: New York: The Harbour of Arrivals
description:
A single narrator tells the story of New York City as a harbour town that grew into a metropolis. It begins with the harbour and the Lenape shore, then Verrazzano and Henry Hudson, Dutch New Amsterdam, and the English takeover in 1664. After that come the Revolution and Washington's inauguration, the Erie Canal, the 1811 grid, the Brooklyn Bridge, Central Park, the Statue of Liberty, Ellis Island, and the five-borough consolidation of 1898. It ends with evening on the harbour.

Chapters: 1. The Harbour; 2. A Ship in the Bay; 3. The English Take the Town; 4. A Canal to the West; 5. A Bridge and a Park; 6. Lady Liberty and the Island of Arrivals; 7. Streets and Sky; 8. Walking the Tip of the Island; 9. Five Boroughs, One Harbour; 10. Markets, Ferries, and Daily Bread; 11. The Grid Fills In; 12. Bridges, Tunnels, and the Modern Port; 13. Soft City Nights; 14. Names on the Land; 15. Evening on the Harbour.

title: Paris: The Island in the River
description:
A single narrator tells the story of Paris from its river islands outward. It begins with the Seine and the Parisii settlement of Lutetia, then Clovis and the Capetians, Notre-Dame, the Louvre fortress, and the Left Bank schools. After a light touch on revolutionary storms, it covers Haussmann's boulevards and the Eiffel Tower, and ends with evening on the quays.

Chapters: 1. The Island in the River; 2. Lutetia; 3. A Capital of Kings; 4. Notre-Dame and the Louvre; 5. Students of the Left Bank; 6. Storm and Smoke; 7. Haussmann's Boulevards; 8. An Iron Tower; 9. Walking the Quays; 10. Markets and Neighbourhoods; 11. Bridges Over the Seine; 12. Stone, Water, and Quiet Hours; 13. From Island Outward; 14. Sainte-Chapelle and Royal Light; 15. The University Quarter in Detail; 16. Revolution's Edge, Softly Told; 17. Shops, Arcades, and Evening Streets; 18. Montmartre and the Northern Height; 19. A City That Reads Itself; 20. Boatmen and the City Motto; 21. Evening on the Seine.

title: Rome: The City of Seven Hills
description:
A single narrator tells the story of Rome from the seven hills beside the Tiber. It begins with the Romulus legend as legend, early kings and the Republic, then aqueducts, the Forum, the Colosseum, and the Pantheon. After a gentle pass through later papal and Italian Rome, it ends with evening among the stones of the Forum.

Chapters: 1. The City of Seven Hills; 2. Legend and Beginning; 3. The Republic; 4. Water on Arches; 5. Forum, Colosseum, Pantheon; 6. Living in the Ancient City; 7. After the Emperors; 8. Walking the Hills; 9. Fountains and Everyday Water; 10. Palatine and Capitoline; 11. Bread, Circuses, and Ordinary Days; 12. Concrete, Arch, and Dome; 13. Pilgrims and the Christian City; 14. Modern Capitals Inside One City; 15. Markets of Trajan and the Crowded Centre; 16. Latin Voices Softly Recalled; 17. Tiber Island and the River's Mood; 18. Quiet Arrival at Night; 19. Ostia and the Mouth of the River; 20. Closing the Day Gently; 21. Aurelian Walls and the City's Edge; 22. Gardens, Villas, and Shade; 23. Evening Among the Stones.

title: Cartagena, Parte 1: La bahía y las murallas
description:
Primera de dos noches en Cartagena de Indias. Un narrador cuenta, sin prisa, la bahía de Calamarí y sus primeros pueblos, la fundación de Pedro de Heredia en 1533, las flotas de la plata, los corsarios y la toma de Francis Drake en 1586. Después siguen el plan de Antonelli, las murallas de piedra coralina, el castillo de San Felipe y el canal del Dique, hasta una tarde tranquila sobre la muralla.

Capítulos: 1. La bahía de Calamarí; 2. Los pueblos antes de la ciudad; 3. Pedro de Heredia; 4. La fundación; 5. Una ciudad de paja y madera; 6. Las flotas de la plata; 7. Hawkins y el Draque; 8. La toma de 1586; 9. El plan de Antonelli; 10. La piedra del mar; 11. La boca que se cerró; 12. El castillo en el cerro de San Lázaro; 13. El barón de Pointis; 14. El canal hacia el gran río; 15. La Popa y la Virgen de la Candelaria; 16. La vida dentro de las murallas; 17. El ritmo del puerto; 18. Una tarde en la muralla.

title: Cartagena, Parte 2: El asedio y la ciudad tranquila
description:
Segunda y última noche en Cartagena de Indias. El asedio británico de 1741 y la defensa de Blas de Lezo, el puerto de los africanos esclavizados, Alonso de Sandoval, Pedro Claver y San Basilio de Palenque, la independencia del 11 de noviembre de 1811 y el sitio de 1815. Después, el largo sueño del siglo XIX y el despertar de la ciudad, y un paseo lento por el centro histórico hasta la noche, con la brisa del mar.

Capítulos: 1. Regreso a la bahía; 2. Una guerra con nombre extraño; 3. Blas de Lezo; 4. La gran armada; 5. Bocachica; 6. La madrugada de San Lázaro; 7. Las lluvias y las medallas; 8. El ingeniero Arévalo; 9. Bocachica hoy; 10. El puerto de los esclavizados; 11. Alonso de Sandoval y Pedro Claver; 12. Palenque; 13. El once de noviembre; 14. La Ciudad Heroica; 15. El largo sueño; 16. Rafael Núñez y el despertar; 17. Un paseo por la ciudad amurallada; 18. La Plaza de Bolívar; 19. Los patios y la brisa; 20. La tarde sobre la muralla; 21. Noche en Cartagena.

title: Antioquia, Parte 1: Oro, arrieros y montañas
description:
Primera de dos partes sobre Antioquia, contada en español por un solo narrador. Recorre las cordilleras y los valles del Cauca y del Magdalena, los pueblos indígenas, la conquista de Jorge Robledo y Santa Fe de Antioquia, el oro de los ríos, la libertad de El Guarzo en El Retiro, los arrieros, la colonización del sur y la llegada del café. Termina en una tarde de neblina en el altiplano del oriente.

Capítulos: 1. Una tierra hecha de montañas; 2. Los primeros pueblos; 3. Robledo y la conquista; 4. Santa Fe de Antioquia; 5. El oro de los ríos; 6. La libertad de El Guarzo; 7. Mon y Velarde y los nuevos pueblos; 8. Rionegro y el altiplano; 9. Los arrieros; 10. Hacia el sur; 11. El café; 12. Los pueblos del suroeste; 13. La casa campesina; 14. La música de las montañas; 15. Los pueblos y sus plazas; 16. Una tarde en el altiplano.

title: Medellín, Parte 2: El valle de la eterna primavera
description:
Segunda parte, dedicada a Medellín y al valle de Aburrá. Empieza con los años difíciles, contados con sobriedad, y con la transformación de la ciudad: el Metro, el Metrocable, los parques biblioteca y las escaleras de la Comuna 13. Luego vuelve a la Villa de la Candelaria de 1675, la capital de 1826, el tren y las fábricas textiles, y sube hasta Santa Elena, los silleteros y la Feria de las Flores. Termina con el valle iluminado y la neblina sobre las montañas.

Capítulos: 1. El valle de Aburrá; 2. Los años difíciles; 3. La transformación; 4. El valle de los aburraes; 5. La Villa de la Candelaria; 6. La nueva capital; 7. El tren y las fábricas; 8. La ciudad crece; 9. Guayaquil y los mercados; 10. La vida de barrio; 11. El jardín botánico; 12. Botero y las plazas del centro; 13. Santa Elena y los silleteros; 14. La Feria de las Flores; 15. Las montañas de Arví; 16. El río del valle; 17. La gente del valle; 18. Una tarde en el valle.

title: Tokyo, Part 1: The Castle Town of Edo
description:
The first of two nights in Tokyo. It opens with Perry's black ships in the bay in 1853, then goes back to the fishing shore of Edo, Ota Dokan's castle of 1457 and Tokugawa Ieyasu's arrival in 1590. From there it follows the shogun's castle town, the lords' processions, the great fire of 1657, the aqueducts, Nihonbashi, the fish market and the floating world, and ends on an ordinary evening by the Sumida River.

Chapters: 1. Black Ships in the Bay; 2. A Village Where the Rivers Meet the Sea; 3. The Castle of Ota Dokan; 4. Ieyasu Comes East; 5. Making Land from Marsh and Hill; 6. The Lords' Long Roads; 7. The Long-Sleeves Fire; 8. Temples and Shrines of the Town; 9. Water for a Million People; 10. Nihonbashi, the Bridge at the Centre; 11. Markets and Morning Fish; 12. The Floating World; 13. The Gardens of the Lords; 14. Seasons Along the River; 15. An Evening in Old Edo.

title: Tokyo, Part 2: The Eastern Capital
description:
The second night in Tokyo follows Edo becoming Tokyo in 1868, the emperor moving into the old castle, the first railway, Ginza's brick town, Tokyo Station and the first subway. It covers the 1923 earthquake and the 1945 fire raids soberly and briefly, then the rebuilding and the 1964 Olympics and Shinkansen. The rest is a slow walk through quiet places you can visit in December: the Meiji Jingu forest, Ueno, Yanaka, the last streetcar, Tsukiji, a neighbourhood bath, winter views of Mount Fuji, the turn of the year, and the Sumida at dusk.

Chapters: 1. The Castle Changes Hands; 2. An Emperor in the East; 3. Steam and Brick; 4. A City of Stations; 5. The Earthquake of 1923; 6. Fire and Rebuilding; 7. The Autumn of 1964; 8. A Forest Planted by a Nation; 9. The Hill at Ueno; 10. The Old Lanes of Yanaka; 11. A Garden by the River; 12. The Last Streetcar; 13. Morning at the Market; 14. The Neighbourhood Bath; 15. Winter Light on the Mountain; 16. The Turning of the Year; 17. The Sumida at Dusk.

title: Hong Kong, Part 1: The Fragrant Harbour
description:
The first of three nights in Hong Kong. A single narrator follows the fragrant harbour from the volcanic fires that shaped its granite hills, through Neolithic shore camps, Tang and Song era salt fields, pearl beds and walled villages, and the boat-dwelling families of the bays. Then come the opium trade, Commissioner Lin, the First Opium War, the landing of January 1841, the Treaty of Nanking, Kowloon in 1860 and the New Territories lease of 1898, before the story settles into a quiet evening on the harbour around 1900.

Chapters: 1. A Harbour Between Mountains; 2. Fire Beneath the Hills; 3. The First People of the Shore; 4. Salt, Pearls, and Incense; 5. The Boy Emperor and the Walled Villages; 6. People of the Water; 7. Tea, Silver, and Opium; 8. The Commissioner and the Sea; 9. The First Opium War; 10. The Treaty of Nanking; 11. Across the Water to Kowloon; 12. The Lease of 1898; 13. Evening on the Harbour.

title: Hong Kong, Part 2: The City Climbs the Hills
description:
The second of three nights in Hong Kong. The colonial town climbs the slopes: the Peak Tram of 1888, the Star Ferry, the plague summer of 1894 told briefly, and Sun Yat-sen's student years. The Japanese occupation of 1941 to 1945 is told soberly, then the postwar refugees, the Shek Kip Mei fire and public housing, the factories of Made in Hong Kong, the new towns, the famous Kai Tak approach and the Kowloon Walled City. It ends in the quiet garden where the Walled City once stood.

Chapters: 1. The Town on the Slopes; 2. A Railway to the Peak; 3. The Summer of 1894; 4. Across the Harbour by Star; 5. A Doctor and a Republic; 6. The Hardest Years; 7. Newcomers on the Hillsides; 8. Made in Hong Kong; 9. Little Shanghai and the Silver Screen; 10. New Towns in the Hills; 11. Kai Tak and the Checkerboard; 12. The Walled City; 13. Evening in Kowloon.

title: Hong Kong, Part 3: The Harbour at Evening
description:
The last of three nights in Hong Kong. The 1984 Joint Declaration and the rainy handover night of 1 July 1997 are told factually, then the story slows into the city as it lives today: the skyline, the ding ding trams, morning dim sum and cha chaan teng cafés, markets and festivals, the country parks, Lantau's Big Buddha and the stilt houses of Tai O, and the car-free outlying islands. It ends on an evening Star Ferry crossing of the harbour.

Chapters: 1. The End of a Lease; 2. The Joint Declaration; 3. The Night of the Handover; 4. A Forest of Towers; 5. Riding the Ding Ding; 6. Morning Tea; 7. Markets and Old Streets; 8. A Year of Festivals; 9. The Green Hills; 10. The Big Island; 11. The Outlying Islands; 12. Evening on the Harbour.

title: Archimedes: The Geometer of Syracuse
description:
The life of Archimedes in his home city of Syracuse, from the Roman fleet broken by his machines in 213 BC to the quiet harbour at evening. It follows the law of the lever and Hiero's great ship, the golden wreath and the bath (a later legend, told by Vitruvius), floating bodies, the water screw, circles and spheres, the siege, Cicero's search for his tomb, and the prayer book that hid his lost writing.

The Water Snail; 9. Circles and Spheres; 10. The Siege of Syracuse; 11. The Bronze Heavens; 12. Cicero Finds the Tomb; 13. The Book Beneath the Prayers; 14. Evening in Syracuse.

title: Thomas Edison, Part 1: The Wizard of Menlo Park
description:
The first of two nights with Thomas Edison. It opens at Menlo Park in December 1877, when a tinfoil machine first speaks back, then goes back to the canal town of Milan, Ohio, the boyhood by the St. Clair River at Port Huron, the newsboy and wandering telegrapher years, and the Newark workshops. From there it follows the invention factory at Menlo Park, the phonograph and the long search for a lasting light bulb in 1879, and ends on a quiet winter evening among the lamps in the snow.

New York and Newark (9:58); 7. The Invention Factory (12:06); 8. The Men of Menlo Park (14:23); 9. The Talking Machine (16:13); 10. The Problem of Light (17:57); 11. A Thread of Carbon (20:33); 12. title: Thomas Edison, Part 2: The Garden at Fort Myers
description:
The second of two nights with Thomas Edison. It opens with the Pearl Street station lighting lower Manhattan in September 1882, then follows the move to the great laboratory at West Orange, the improved phonograph, the quarrel over alternating current, the iron mine, and the first motion pictures in the Black Maria. It ends at his winter home on the Caloosahatchee River at Fort Myers, in the garden at dusk.

title: Nikola Tesla, Part 1: The Rotating Field
description:
The first of two nights with Nikola Tesla. It opens in Budapest's City Park in 1882, where by his own account the idea of the rotating magnetic field came to him, then goes back to the village of Smiljan in Lika, school in Karlovac, Graz and Prague, and the telephone exchange in Budapest. From there it follows Paris and Strasbourg, his arrival in New York in 1884, the lean years, the alternating current motor, and his partnership with George Westinghouse, and ends on a quiet evening in his Manhattan laboratory.

The Telephone Exchange (9:53); 7. Paris and Strasbourg (11:14); 8. Arrival in New York (13:01); 9. The Lean Year (14:45); 10. The Motor Takes Shape (16:17); 11. Westinghouse (17:44); 12. The Royalty (21:05); 13. The Laboratory at Night (22:29); 14. A Man of Habits (23:50); 15. Evening on South Fifth Avenue (25:17).

title: Leonardo da Vinci, Part 1: The Boy from Vinci
description:
The first of three nights with Leonardo da Vinci. It opens with an unfinished Saint Jerome, then goes back to the hill town of Vinci in 1452 and the young man's apprenticeship in Andrea del Verrocchio's busy Florentine workshop. From the golden ball on the cathedral dome and his first dated landscape drawing to the angel in the Baptism of Christ, Ginevra de' Benci and the unfinished Adoration of the Magi, it follows him to his move to Milan around 1482, and ends on an evening on the Lombard plain.

Chapters: 1. A Panel Cut in Pieces; 2. The Town on the Hill; 3. A Childhood Among the Olives; 4. The City on the Arno; 5. The Drawings Shown to Verrocchio; 6. The Workshop of Andrea del Verrocchio; 7. Tobias and the Little Dog; 8. The Golden Ball on the Dome; 9. The Day of Santa Maria della Neve; 10. The Angel in the Corner; 11. Ginevra and the Juniper; 12. A Shield and a Cave; 13. Florence in Uneasy Years; 14. The Adoration of the Magi; 15. The Silver Lyre; 16. The Road North; 17. Evening on the Plain.

title: Nikola Tesla, Part 2: The Power of Niagara
description:
The second of two nights with Nikola Tesla. It opens with artificial lightning on the Colorado prairie in 1899, then goes back to the White City of the 1893 Chicago fair, the fire that destroyed his laboratory, and the harnessing of Niagara Falls, with power reaching Buffalo in November 1896. From there it follows Colorado Springs, the unfinished tower at Wardenclyffe, and the hotel years with his beloved pigeons, and ends on a quiet autumn night beside the falls.

Chapters: 1. Lightning on the Prairie (0:14); 2. The White City (2:02); 3. The Egg of Columbus (4:20); 4. The Fire on South Fifth Avenue (5:45); 5. A Picture of Niagara (7:13); 6. The Choice of Current (9:20); 7. The Powerhouse (10:55); 8. Power for Buffalo (12:26); 9. Colorado Springs (13:51); 10. A Summer in the Mountains (15:16); 11. The Tower at Wardenclyffe (16:43); 12. Old Friends (19:03); 13. The Hotel Years (20:35); 14. The Pigeons (23:18); 15. The Unit of Light and Power (24:33); 16. Niagara at Night (25:31).

title: Galileo Galilei, Part 1: The Starry Messenger
description:
The first of two nights with Galileo. It opens on a cold January night in Padua in 1610, when three small points of light beside Jupiter began to move, then goes back to Pisa: a musician's son, the swinging lamp and the leaning tower (both stories told gently as uncertain), and the long, happy years in Padua with balls rolling down slopes. It follows the spyglass from Holland to the bell tower of Saint Mark's, the mountains of the Moon, the Starry Messenger of 1610, and ends in a quiet garden in Padua under the winter stars.

Chapters: 1. Three Small Stars; 2. A Musician's Son in Pisa; 3. The Student of Medicine; 4. The Swinging Lamp; 5. Falling Bodies; 6. The Road to Padua; 7. A House in Padua; 8. Balls on a Slope; 9. News from Holland; 10. Grinding Glass; 11. The Face of the Moon; 12. The Starry Messenger; 13. Court Mathematician; 14. More Wonders in the Sky; 15. A Visit to Rome; 16. A Clear Night over Padua.

title: Galileo Galilei, Part 2: The Villa at Arcetri
description:
The second of two nights with Galileo. It begins with the morning in June 1633 when he knelt before the Roman Inquisition, then goes back to tell, factually and calmly, how he came there: Florence, the letters on scripture, the decree of 1616, the Dialogue and its cabin below decks, and the trial. Then it slows into his last years under house arrest at Arcetri, his daughter Maria Celeste, Two New Sciences and the pendulum clock, and ends on a spring evening on the Tuscan hills above Florence.

Chapters: 1. A Morning in June; 2. Return to Florence; 3. Ice and Ebony; 4. Letters on Scripture; 5. The Decree of 1616; 6. A Clock in the Sky; 7. The Assayer; 8. A Dialogue in Four Days; 9. The Cabin Below Decks; 10. The Summons; 11. A Famous Phrase; 12. Siena and the Road Home; 13. Two New Sciences; 14. Darkness and Visitors; 15. Days at Il Gioiello; 16. The Villa on the Hill; 17. Evening at Arcetri.

title: Leonardo da Vinci, Part 2: The Horse and the Supper
description:
The second of three nights with Leonardo da Vinci, his eighteen years in Milan under Ludovico Sforza. It opens with his remarkable letter to the duke offering war machines, bridges and, almost as an afterthought, painting. Then it follows the Virgin of the Rocks, the Lady with an Ermine, the great clay horse whose bronze became cannon, the Last Supper and the notebooks on flight, water and anatomy, and ends quietly in the vineyard the duke gave him.

Chapters: 1. A Letter to the Duke; 2. The Moor of Milan; 3. A City on Two Levels; 4. The Virgin of the Rocks; 5. A Festival of Planets; 6. The Lady with an Ermine; 7. The Little Devil; 8. Fables and Riddles; 9. The Great Horse; 10. Bronze for Cannon; 11. The Refectory Wall; 12. The Prior's Complaint; 13. The Notebooks; 14. Wings and Water; 15. Inside the Body; 16. A Ceiling of Mulberry Trees; 17. The Fall of the Moor; 18. The Vineyard.

title: Zhang Heng and Su Song: The Dragon Jar and the Clock Tower
description:
Two Chinese scholars nine centuries apart. Zhang Heng, the Han dynasty astronomer and poet, shows the court his bronze earthquake detector in AD 132, writes his rhapsodies on the capitals and turns a model of the heavens by water. Then Su Song builds his great water-driven clock tower at Kaifeng in the 1090s, with its escapement, armillary sphere and little figures announcing the hours. It ends in the quiet observatory garden at Gaocheng.

Chapters: 1. The Dragon and the Toad; 2. A Boy from Nanyang; 3. Rhapsodies on the Capitals; 4. The Chief Astronomer; 5. How the Dragon Knew; 6. Return to the Fields; 7. Nine Hundred Years; 8. Su Song of Quanzhou; 9. The Emperor's Clock; 10. Inside the Tower; 11. The Book and the Lost Tower; 12. The Observatory Garden.

title: Leonardo da Vinci, Part 3: The River at Amboise
description:
The last of three nights with Leonardo da Vinci, through his wandering years. It opens with Cesare Borgia's passport naming him architect and general engineer, then follows the map of Imola, the plan to move the Arno, the lost Battle of Anghiari and the portrait of Lisa del Giocondo. From the anatomy drawings and the notebook on the flight of birds to Rome and a mechanical lion for the King of France, it ends at Clos Lucé in Amboise, on the Loire at evening.

Chapters: 1. Architect and General Engineer; 2. Leaving Milan; 3. The Cartoon of Saint Anne; 4. The Map of Imola; 5. The Envoy from Florence; 6. Moving a River; 7. The Battle of Anghiari; 8. The Wife of Francesco del Giocondo; 9. Birds over Fiesole; 10. The Anatomist; 11. Why the Moon Glows; 12. Rome; 13. A Lion for the King; 14. The House at Cloux; 15. Saint John Pointing Upward; 16. Last Plans; 17. Spring in Amboise; 18. The Scattered Pages; 19. The Loire at Evening.

title: The Wright Brothers: The Bicycle Makers Who Flew
description:
The Wright brothers, from a Dayton bicycle shop to the first powered flights. It opens on the freezing morning of 17 December 1903 at Kill Devil Hills, then goes back to the bishop's boys, the toy helicopter, the printing press and the bicycle shop. It follows the twisted inner-tube box, the gliders at Kitty Hawk, the homemade wind tunnel and Charlie Taylor's engine to the circles over Huffman Prairie, and ends on the quiet dunes at evening.

Chapters: 1. A Cold Morning by the Sea; 2. Twelve Seconds; 3. The Bishop's Boys; 4. A Hockey Stick and a Printing Press; 5. The Bicycle Shop; 6. The House on Hawthorn Street; 7. The Death of Otto Lilienthal; 8. A Twist of Cardboard; 9. Kitty Hawk; 10. Not Within a Thousand Years; 11. The Wind Tunnel; 12. The Glider That Flew; 13. Charlie Taylor's Engine; 14. Months in the Sand; 15. Huffman Prairie; 16. October Over the Pasture; 17. The Dunes at Evening.

title: Johannes Gutenberg: The Press in Mainz
description:
How a goldsmith of Mainz made the first great printed book in Europe. It follows Johannes Gutenberg from the patrician families of Mainz to his secret venture in Strasbourg, the punches, moulds, type metal and press, the 42-line Bible of around 1455, and the lawsuit with Johann Fust that cost him his workshop. Then it traces how printing spread across Europe, and ends in a quiet print shop at dusk.

Chapters: 1. Pages at the Frankfurt Fair; 2. The Patrician of Mainz; 3. The Venture in Strasbourg; 4. The Problem of the Letters; 5. The Workshop at the Humbrechthof; 6. How a Page Was Printed; 7. The Great Bible; 8. Fust and the Lawsuit; 9. The Quiet Years; 10. How Print Spread; 11. What the Press Changed; 12. Evening in the Print Shop.
